subject.title: Add an FxTwitter read transport for public lookups, threads, profiles, and search

question: Should Birdclaw core officially support FxTwitter/FxEmbed as an opt-in public read transport, including the associated privacy disclosure and third-party reliability commitment?
rationale: The existing architecture can accommodate another read transport, but source inspection cannot decide whether the repository owner wants a public hosted service and its long-term operational contract in core.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow MVP
options.body: Approve an explicitly selected public-read adapter with capability gating, validated HTTPS endpoints, provenance, fixtures, and no automatic fallback.

options.title: Defer core integration
options.body: Leave the request open but defer implementation until the service contract or Birdclaw’s external transport-extension boundary is clearer.

options.title: Decline hosted-service support
options.body: Keep core limited to the existing authenticated transports and local archives, allowing only an independently maintained integration if a suitable extension surface emerges.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow MVP
recommendation.body: Approve an explicitly selected public-read adapter with capability gating, validated HTTPS endpoints, provenance, fixtures, and no automatic fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes Birdclaw’s supported transport, privacy, configuration, and operational boundaries and therefore belongs with the repository owner.
